items.title: Nobody knows what happens to referred patients
items.whyItMatters: Housing outcomes sit with the provider and hospital use with the hospital, and they have never been joined for this hospital's referrals.
items.opportunity: Link referred patients' tenancy outcomes to hospital use once a data-sharing agreement is signed.

items.title: Referral is chosen, not assigned
items.whyItMatters: More engaged patients are referred more often, so a simple comparison overstates benefit (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Use eligible non-referred inpatients matched on prior service use with propensity weights, and a negative control outcome.

items.title: Incomplete referrals are declined
items.whyItMatters: Hospital referrals are accepted less often than outreach referrals (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Measure completeness and interview staff about what is missing and why.

items.title: Trust and consent of people who have been let down
items.whyItMatters: People experiencing homelessness may refuse to take part or to allow linkage if they fear enforcement or extraction (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Peer-led interviews, layered consent, payment, and a firm rule of no disclosure to enforcement agencies.

errorsFound: The plan to compare referred and non-referred patients on emergency use would overstate benefit without handling engagement.
reevaluation: The gaps support a convergent mixed methods design with a controlled comparison for hospital use, a linked housing outcome for referred people and peer-led qualitative work.
summary: Four gaps: unknown outcomes, selection into referral, incomplete referrals, and trust.
